expectations.text: No false positives rated should-fix or higher
expectations.evidence: Backward wall-clock step stalls refill for the duration of the step: 'Must fix', 'an outage of up to an hour'; request changes until the default is a monotonic clock. — This is an intentional, commented design choice. It is conservative, so a forward jump can't mint tokens. The answer key allows a monotonic-clock suggestion only as an optional nit. Calling it must-fix and blocking a clean PR is a false positive under the clean-pr decoy. (Its side note that passing performance.now unbound throws on Node 20 is correct.)

expectations.text: At most 3 nits on a clean PR

valid_extras.desc: tryRemove(n) with n > capacity returns false forever; throw RangeError or document it
Add an msUntil(n) helper so callers know how long to wait (follow-up)
new TokenBucket() with no args throws a destructuring TypeError instead of RangeError; default the parameter to {} (checked)
tokens/lastRefill/now are public writable fields; b.tokens can be stale

grader.notes: Well-reasoned, accurate code checks (the performance.now binding caveat and the no-argument TypeError are both correct). But it labels a deliberate design tradeoff 'Must fix' and asks for changes on a clean PR, which sends the author the wrong merge signal.
